A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Proxy-GS, with matching core algorithms, benchmarks, and extensive appendix material. All pages, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering experiments, quantitative benchmark comparisons, component ablations, timing analyses, and qualitative results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and adds proxy-fidelity experiments and comparisons of alternative depth sources.

M1.justification: The reported indoor proxy-construction procedure changes from monocular depth estimation with MoGe2 and PGSR refinement to MapAnything using RGB images and COLMAP inputs (Section 4.2; v1 Appendix A.4.2 versus v3 Appendix 7.5.2). The core occlusion filtering, proxy-guided densification, and rendering pipeline remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage remains MatrixCity, Zip-NeRF/Berlin, Small City, and CUHK-LOWER for novel-view synthesis. v3 additionally evaluates deliberately corrupted proxy inputs on Block 5, introducing a limited input-quality scenario through vertex-noise perturbations.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix 7.3 and Table 6 add nvdiffrast and depth extracted from a pretrained 3DGS model as alternatives to the proposed depth source. The comparator sets in the retained benchmark and renderer-integration experiments are unchanged; newly discussed related methods are not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New Block 5 protocols vary proxy resolution across 100%, 10%, 5%, and 1%, and vertex noise across 0%, 5%, 10%, and 20%, alongside depth-source substitutions. Existing partitions, metrics, 40k training iterations, and A100/RTX 4090 hardware settings are retained. Indoor preprocessing is reported differently, without establishing which retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends validation of the central proxy dependency through mesh-resolution and vertex-noise sensitivity studies, mesh and rendering visualizations, and alternative-depth-source comparisons (Figures 5-7 and Appendix 7.3). The previous training-component, safety-margin, timing, and renderer-integration analyses remain; the safety-margin study moves to the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Random vertex perturbations in v3 do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark tables, ablations, hardware-renderer results, anchor counts, and timing results are unchanged. Substantial new findings concern proxy sensitivity: Figure 7 shows approximately stable 21.7 dB PSNR under simplification but a decline to approximately 16.7 dB at 20% vertex noise. New Table 6 reports 32, 54, and 151 FPS for nvdiffrast, 3DGS, and the proposed approach in the depth-source comparison.

T1.justification: The substantive culling and densification mathematics and the appendix QEM and Hi-Z derivations are retained. v3 omits the routine camera/clip/NDC conversion explanation in v1 Equations 2-4, but introduces no changed mathematical reasoning, assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the explicit claim of rendering faster than original 3DGS and retains the comparison against Octree-GS. The central contributions—shared proxy guidance for training and inference, improved rendering quality and speed, and sub-millisecond depth acquisition—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 explains why simplification preserves useful occlusion structure in largely planar urban scenes, whereas vertex noise disrupts boundaries and creates rendering artifacts. It qualifies the earlier general robustness discussion with limited effects below the tested 5% noise level and substantial degradation at larger perturbations.

D1.justification: v3 updates indoor mesh-construction instructions and specifies proxy-fidelity test levels and mesh sizes from 108 MB to 824 KB. It removes the explicit projection equations and numerical stabilizer documented in v1, along with promises to release code and trained models. Most hardware and implementation details remain; the PDFs do not establish an actual change in public resource availability.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against recent work, including LODGE, Horizon-GS, Virtualized 3D Gaussians, VastGaussian, and OccluGaussian. It removes v1's first-to-address-occlusion-redundancy assertion and explicitly distinguishes per-pixel proxy filtering from OccluGaussian's clustering. Indoor reconstruction references also shift from MoGe2/PGSR-related approaches to MapAnything and VGGT.

P1.justification: The title and author ordering change, selected passages are shortened or rewritten, and the safety-margin discussion moves to the appendix. Reproducibility, ethics, and LLM-use statements disappear. Most of the introduction, method narrative, experimental discussion, and conclusion remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a single-column layout to two columns with separately paginated supplementary material. v3 adds Figures 5-7 and the depth-source table, restyles the timing chart, reorders Table 2's dataset columns, and relocates the previous safety-margin figure and table to appendix Figure 8 and Table 10.

improvement.justification: The new proxy-fidelity studies provide useful evidence for a previously largely asserted robustness property and expose a concrete failure condition. Added depth-source comparisons and more precise positioning strengthen the paper. These gains are limited by incompletely specified perturbation and timing protocols, reduced release information, and unchanged main benchmark evidence, yielding a limited overall improvement.
